alerts.reason: Year-over-year net sales growth slowed from 39.43% in Q1 to 18.36% in Q2 (A), while inventory rose about 68%, from $202 million to $339 million (C). The Q2 sales cushion supports a Q3 forecast above -5.00%, but inventory growing that much faster than sales raises the risk that holiday markdowns push Q4 net sales to a decline of at least 5.00%.

Net sales growth slowed from 18.61% in Q1 to 11.98% in Q2 despite a roughly two-point Q2 lift from Anniversary Sale timing (E). Resilience among higher-income customers supports a Q3 forecast above -5.00%. Demand was already softening more sharply among lower-income customers across both banners (D), creating a risk of a decline of at least 5.00% in the holiday quarter (A).

Year-over-year sales growth slowed from 17.08% in April to 9.58% in July (A). Another 7.5-point slowdown in each of the next two quarters would put growth near +2.1% in the intervening quarter and -5.4% in the target quarter. Disrupted campus buybacks constrained the supply of used textbooks for future selling periods (C), supporting the forecast of further slowing.
